course_name_original: Elasticidad y Resistencia de Materiales II
course_name_en: Elasticity and Strength of Materials II
prerequisites: Knowledge, understanding, and application of the principles, concepts, and hypotheses of mechanics and related subjects.
Knowledge of the mechanical characteristics of plane sections (area, center of gravity, and moments of inertia).
Free body diagram. Static equilibrium equations. Action, reaction, and stresses.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Apply appropriate failure criteria (Von Mises, Tresca, etc.) to determine the safety factor of a mechanical component subjected to multiaxial loads.

syllabus_topics: RM1: Axial Stress. Tension and Compression: Stress analysis section, Deformation analysis, Energy analysis, Articulated structures, Sizing, Hyperstatic bars.
RM2: Bending I. Shear forces and Bending moment: Stress analysis, Types of joints, Sizing.
RM3-4: Bending II. Pure and Compound Bending: Stress analysis, Sizing.
RM5: Bending III. Deformations in Bending: General hypotheses, Elastic differential equation, Rotation law and elastic equation, Mohr's theorems, Energy theorems.
RM6: Bending IV. Simple Bending: Stress analysis, Sizing.
RM7: Torsion: Circular section, Non-circular and thin sections, Flexo-torsion. Combination of stresses.
RM8: Combination of stresses: Combined stresses, Concept of limit state, Safety factor.
RM9: Buckling: Stability analysis, Critical load, Sizing.
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes (Exposition of contents by the teaching staff).
Practical classes (Group work sessions supervised by the teaching staff. Significant construction of knowledge through interaction and student activity).
Laboratory (Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics).

Seminars/Workshops (Monographic sessions supervised and with shared participation. Conferences/Seminars by experts, Company visits, Attendance at fairs, Attendance at workshops/congresses, Debates, Seminars for developing specific or transversal competencies).
Team Work / Integrated Project (Realization of a project to solve a problem or tackle a task through planning, design, and execution of a series of activities).

Tutorials (Personalized and small group attention. Instruction carried out with the objective of reviewing, redirecting class materials, learning, and carrying out assignments, etc. Specific student inquiries. Scheduled tutorials).
Group work (Individual and group preparation of essays, problem solving, projects, etc., to be submitted and presented in practical classes).
Individual / Autonomous work (Student study: preparation of readings, preparation of exams, preparation of exercises, preparation of classes, etc.).
assessment_rules: The final grade is obtained by weighting the written test at 60%, practice reports/problems at 15%, and the Integrated Project at 25%. It is essential to obtain a minimum average grade of 4 in the written tests to average with other components. The course is considered approved if the final grade is 5 or higher and no written part grade is below 4 points. In the first call, unapproved parts can be retaken. In the second call, Integrated Project scores are maintained.
